title: Sixth Word Conclusion Ease Of The Sale Lawful Bounds And Servanthood

questions.question: What question is asked at the start of the passage about giving back the trust to its Owner?
questions.answer: It asks whether doing this is really hard or too heavy for people.

questions.question: How does the passage answer that question?
questions.answer: It says it is not hard at all.

questions.question: Why does the passage say people do not need to cross the limits set by Allah?
questions.answer: Because what is allowed is wide enough for human wants.

questions.question: How are Allah’s duties described in this passage?
questions.answer: They are described as light and not many.

questions.question: What two roles are used to describe a believer serving Allah?
questions.answer: A believer is described as a servant and a soldier.

questions.question: How is serving Allah described emotionally?
questions.answer: It is described as a great honor full of deep happiness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is a person’s simple duty in life?
questions.answer: To begin actions in Allah’s name and live by His permission and law.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about taking and giving?
questions.answer: A person should take and give for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about movement and stillness?
questions.answer: A person should act or refrain from acting according to Allah’s rules.

questions.question: If a person fails in these duties, what should he do next?
questions.answer: He should ask Allah to forgive him.

questions.question: Besides asking forgiveness, what else should a person ask from Allah?
questions.answer: He should ask to be accepted as Allah’s servant and to be helped to guard the trust faithfully.

questions.question: Until when should a person ask to be a trustworthy keeper of the trust?
questions.answer: Until the time comes for that trust to be taken back.

questions.question: What is the main point of this passage?
questions.answer: Living by Allah’s rules is not too hard, and when a person slips, he should turn back to Allah.

questions.question: Which is wider in this passage: what Allah allows or what He forbids?
questions.answer: What Allah allows is wider.

questions.question: What does that teach a Muslim child about temptation?
questions.answer: It teaches that we do not need haram because Allah has already given many halal choices.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number and weight of Allah’s commands?
questions.answer: They are few and easy enough to carry.

questions.question: Why might calling a believer a soldier be a helpful image here?
questions.answer: It shows obedience, discipline, and following orders for a higher purpose.

questions.question: What does doing things in Allah’s name mean in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means making your actions for Him and remembering Him in what you do.

questions.question: How should a person handle both receiving things and giving things?
questions.answer: He should do both in a way that pleases Allah.

questions.question: What rule should guide a person’s actions according to the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s permission and His law should guide them.

questions.question: Does the passage expect people to be perfect all the time?
questions.answer: No. It shows that people may fall short and then should repent.

questions.question: In the prayer at the end, what is being asked about the trust?
questions.answer: The person asks to protect it faithfully until Allah takes it back.

questions.question: What feeling about Allah’s commands does the passage try to remove?
questions.answer: It tries to remove the feeling that obeying Allah is too difficult.

questions.question: What reason is given to show that obedience is manageable?
questions.answer: The allowed things are plenty, so there is no need to go into the forbidden.

questions.question: If someone says, “Allah asks too much,” which line of thought from the passage answers that?
questions.answer: The passage answers that Allah’s duties are light and limited.

questions.question: What honorable relationship to Allah is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Being His servant and His soldier.

questions.question: Why is that relationship not described as shameful?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a joyful honor.

questions.question: What kind of life does the passage encourage: self-ruled or Allah-ruled?
questions.answer: Allah-ruled.

questions.question: Name one everyday area the passage says should be connected to Allah.
questions.answer: Taking and giving.

questions.question: Name another everyday area the passage says should be connected to Allah.
questions.answer: Moving and stopping.

questions.question: What should a person do after noticing he has not fully obeyed?
questions.answer: He should ask Allah to pardon him.

questions.question: What two requests are made after asking for pardon?
questions.answer: To be accepted as a servant and to be made trustworthy in keeping the trust.

questions.question: At the beginning, what false idea about this “trade” is rejected?
questions.answer: The false idea that it is too hard and too heavy.

questions.question: What makes the burden lighter according to the passage: many restrictions or broad permission?
questions.answer: Broad permission makes it lighter.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the halal choices Allah gave people?
questions.answer: They are broad and enough for people.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is doing haram unnecessary?
questions.answer: Because halal already covers people’s needs and desires.

questions.question: How are Allah’s responsibilities for us described in size and amount?
questions.answer: They are small in burden and few in number.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to explain a Muslim’s mission in life?
questions.answer: It uses the picture of a soldier serving under Allah.

questions.question: What does a soldier-like believer do with his actions?
questions.answer: He starts them for Allah and follows Allah’s command.

questions.question: How should choices about giving and receiving be made?
questions.answer: They should be made for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: What should decide whether a person acts or holds back?
questions.answer: Allah’s permission and law.

questions.question: What should happen after a shortcoming: hiding it or turning to Allah?
questions.answer: Turning to Allah.

questions.question: What does the prayer ask Allah to do with our mistakes?
questions.answer: To forgive them.

questions.question: What future help does the prayer ask for regarding the trust?
questions.answer: It asks Allah to help us keep it safely until He takes it back.

questions.question: What answer does the passage give to people who avoid this path because they think it is hard?
questions.answer: It tells them they are mistaken because the path is not truly hard.

questions.question: What is one reason the passage gives for this answer?
questions.answer: Allah has made the lawful wide and sufficient.

questions.question: What does “no need to trespass” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: It means there is no need to do what Allah has forbidden.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the religious duties Allah placed on people?
questions.answer: They are easy enough and not too many.

questions.question: What does the passage say about being Allah’s servant and soldier?
questions.answer: It says this is a wonderful and joyful honor.

questions.question: What is the basic job of a believer according to the passage?
questions.answer: To live, act, and make choices in Allah’s name.

questions.question: Which parts of life are directly mentioned as needing to follow Allah’s guidance?
questions.answer: Taking, giving, moving, and being still.

questions.question: What two guides should shape those parts of life?
questions.answer: Allah’s permission and His law.

questions.question: What should a person admit if he falls short?
questions.answer: He should admit his faults before Allah.

questions.question: After admitting faults, to whom should the person turn?
questions.answer: To Allah.

questions.question: In the prayer, what relationship with Allah does the person ask to have?
questions.answer: He asks to be accepted as Allah’s servant.

questions.question: What does the final prayer teach about responsibility?
questions.answer: It teaches that our trust is serious and we need Allah’s help to carry it faithfully.

questions.question: What two questions open this passage?
questions.answer: They ask whether handing back the trust is difficult and whether it is so heavy that people avoid it.

questions.question: What strong reply is given right after those questions?
questions.answer: A very firm no.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the space Allah gave in lawful things?
questions.answer: It says that space is wide and enough for human desire.

questions.question: What conclusion should a reader make from that about forbidden things?
questions.answer: A reader should understand that going into forbidden things is not needed.

questions.question: How does the passage help calm fear about religious duties?
questions.answer: It says the duties are light and few.

questions.question: What title of honor is given to the one who serves Allah?
questions.answer: The honor of being Allah’s servant and soldier.

questions.question: What is one sign that this service is good for a person, not harmful?
questions.answer: The passage says it brings a special joy and honor.

questions.question: What is the simple rule for starting actions?
questions.answer: Start them in Allah’s name.

questions.question: What is the simple rule for everyday exchanges with others?
questions.answer: Take and give on Allah’s behalf.

questions.question: What is the simple rule for action and rest?
questions.answer: Do both according to Allah’s permission and law.

questions.question: What should come after a mistake: giving up or seeking forgiveness?
questions.answer: Seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: What three things are asked for in the closing prayer?
questions.answer: Forgiveness for faults, acceptance as Allah’s servants, and help in guarding the trust until its time ends.
